Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
32-year-old man with 4-day history of sore throat, nasal congestion, and new dry cough; features most consistent with viral upper respiratory tract infection/early influenza.  

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sore throat and runny nose for 4 days, now improving; dry, constant cough began yesterday.  
• Associated symptoms: Nasal congestion, fatigue, night sweats, generalized headaches (intermittent), myalgias, mild exertional dyspnea, initial fever responsive to paracetamol/ibuprofen. No chest pain, ear pain, vision changes, photophobia, nausea, vomiting, bowel or urinary issues, skin rash.  
• Pertinent negatives: No chest pain, no significant shortness of breath at rest, no nausea/vomiting, no rash.  
• Past medical history: Denies chronic illnesses.  
• Medications: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented); Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Allergies: Denies medication allergies.  
• Family history: Grandmother – type 2 diabetes; great-grandfather – eczema.  
• Social history: Lives alone; accountant; occasional cigar smoking; occasional alcohol intake; no illicit drugs reported. Preventive care not discussed.

Examination:
• Vitals: Not obtained.  
• Physical exam: Not performed (remote consult).

Impression:
Likely viral upper respiratory tract infection (possible early influenza).

Plan:
• Supportive care: Rest, adequate hydration, continue paracetamol and ibuprofen as needed.  
• Work: Advise 1–2 days off for recovery.  
• Red-flag advice: Seek earlier review for high or persistent fever, increasing shortness of breath, chest pain, or if no improvement by next week.  
• Follow-up: Return visit or phone consult if symptoms persist beyond 7 days or worsen.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: Objective vitals, physical examination, full medication list, vaccination status.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor conversational noise, no inaudible sections.
